title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Page 20 of the 8 June 1986 notes for Chapter III, 'Réseaux via découpages'. This is Grothendieck's late attempt to axiomatize a 'topologie modérée' (tame topology), the programme announced in the Esquisse d'un programme. Here it is done inside an ordered 'tronçon' L (an ordered segment or poset). Its closed tame parts ('parties fermées modérées') form a family with a join operation X ∪_mod Y. This join is the least closed tame part containing X and Y, defined for parts in tame general position (previous page). It need not equal the set-theoretic union; the example given is [a,b] ∪_mod [b,c] = [a,c].

(1) Top of page, end of an argument. For every b in L one has L_{≤b} ∪_mod L_{≥b} = L. Hence L is totally ordered if and only if, for all b, every other element is comparable to b. Equivalently, for all b, L_{≤b} ∪_mod L_{≥b} = L_{≤b} ∪ L_{≥b}: the tame join of the down-set and up-set coincides with their naive union.

(2) New heading: 'Parties localement fermées modérées' (tame locally closed parts). Theorem, after a struck-out first attempt:
- Hypotheses: let X ⊃ Y be closed tame parts in tame relative position.
- Set C_mod(Y,X) = {x ∈ X : x ∉ Y, and x is in tame relative position with Y}. This is the 'tame complement' of Y in X.
- Claim: there is a smallest closed tame Z ⊂ X containing C_mod(Y,X), or equivalently containing every closed tame T ⊂ X with T ∩ Y = ∅ and T in tame relative position with Y.
- Moreover Z is in tame position with Y.
- A margin note proposes the notation Z = X ∖_mod Y.

Next page continues: the relative frontier F of Y in X is finite and tame, F ⊂ Z, F contains no isolated points of Z, and C_mod(Y,X) = C_mod(F,Z). Grothendieck then switches (9 June) to the order topology on L and to specialization (b ∈ closure{a} iff b ⊃ a).

In modern terms this is the construction of a 'tame closure of the difference', i.e. the closure of the locally closed set X∖Y. It is part of building a lattice-theoretic calculus of closed and locally closed tame sets, analogous to the closure and frontier operations on definable sets in o-minimal geometry. The purpose is to have a calculus of tame strata for 'découpages' (dissections) of surfaces and of nets.
errors: No proof is given for the existence of the smallest closed tame Z. The hypotheses are partly struck through and reformulated, so the statement is a working draft rather than a finished theorem.
The notion 'x in tame relative position with Y' for a single point x is not defined on this page, so C_mod(Y,X) is only heuristically specified.
The opening criterion for total order is essentially tautological once L_{≤b} ∪_mod L_{≥b} = L is known. That identity is asserted ('vrai pour ∀ b'), not proved here.

ideas.what: Join of closed tame parts (∪_mod), differing from set union, used to characterize total orders via L_{≤b} ∪_mod L_{≥b} = L_{≤b} ∪ L_{≥b}
ideas.modern_name: join in a lattice of closed sets / closure of union; comparability criterion for linear order

ideas.what: Tame difference X ∖_mod Y: smallest closed tame Z ⊂ X containing the points of X∖Y in tame position with Y, with Z in tame position with Y
ideas.modern_name: closure of a locally closed definable set / frontier calculus in o-minimal geometry
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of tame topology is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5

ideas.what: Relative frontier of Y in X is finite and has no isolated points of Z; C_mod(Y,X)=C_mod(F,Z) (next page)
ideas.modern_name: frontier condition / dimension drop of frontier in tame stratifications

missed.claim: An axiomatic, order- and lattice-theoretic approach to tame topology. It works with closed tame parts, tame joins, tame differences and a notion of 'tame relative position', rather than with definable sets from a first-order structure. It was being developed in 1986 independently of the contemporaneous o-minimality work, and was never completed or published.
missed.quote: Soit C_mod(Y,X)={x∈X | x∉Y, x en pos. rel. mod. avec Y} Alors ∃ plus petit ens. fermé modéré Z
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a documented trace of Grothendieck's own concrete attempt at the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse. Historians comparing his programme with o-minimality may find it of interest. Mathematically the content is routine relative to o-minimal geometry.

deep.surprise_reason: Exploratory, partly struck-out foundations of a tame-topology calculus. The results are standard analogues of closure and frontier facts in o-minimal geometry. The interest is mainly historical, as a trace of Grothendieck's own attempt at the tame-topology programme.
transcription_corrections: 'deux p. f.[?]' is likely 'deux p. f. m.' (parties fermées modérées).
The hypothesis line reads 'X ⊃ Y (donc fermées modérées, X et Y en pos. relative modérée)'; 'avec' is struck out.
The margin note 'Ou Z = X∖_mod Y pos' is probably 'On note Z = X ∖_mod Y' (or 'On pose').
'T de 𝓛[?]' is probably a struck '∀' plus 'T' introducing the clause: Z ⊇ T for every closed tame T ⊂ X with T∩Y=∅ in tame relative position with Y.
'tel le que Y' is followed by a struck-out phrase; the remaining insertion is 'De plus, Z est en position modérée avec Y'.
